name: Classen Luxury Apartments (YSA Investments / Vesta Realty)
locationJurisdiction: Oklahoma City, OK (W.D. Okla. Court / Court Receiver David Rhodes)
primaryCause: Elevator System Collapse ($1.7M) & Ownership Dispute (Vesta vs YSA)
sourceName: Oklahoma City Local News & W.D. Okla. Bankruptcy Court Receiver
summary: Oklahoma City luxury high-rise property entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy and court receivership under David Rhodes following severe elevator failure ($1.7M replacement cost), mold/water leaks, and ongoing legal battle between Vesta Realty and YSA Investments.
earlyWarningSignals: 2026-06-15: Court appointed receiver David Rhodes took control from manager Vesta Realty.
2026-05-10: Failed $1.7M replacement project for all four high-rise elevator banks.
2026-04-18: Legal dispute between manager Vesta Realty (CEO Mark Kulik) and owner YSA Investments.
timeline: August 12, 2026 @ 08:00 EST: Chapter 11 Filing & Receivership Update — Tenants report unaddressed elevator failures.
June 15, 2026 @ 10:00 EST: Court Receiver Appointed — David Rhodes takes control of property from Vesta Realty.
May 02, 2026 @ 14:30 EST: Ownership Dispute — Litigation intensifies between Vesta Realty (CEO Mark Kulik) and YSA Investments.

name: WeWork Inc.
locationJurisdiction: New York, NY (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D.N.J.)
primaryCause: Debt Overload & Over-Leasing
summary: Flexible workspace provider that accumulated massive long-term lease liabilities backed by short-term member revenues, leading to unsustainable cash burn and governance collapse.
earlyWarningSignals: 2023-08-08: Issued SEC 'Substantial Doubt' going concern warning.
2023-05-18: Sudden resignation of CEO Sandeep Mathrani.
2023-03-17: Restructuring agreement with SoftBank to swap $1.5B debt for equity.

timeline.title: Peak $47B Valuation
timeline.description: SoftBank Vision Fund leads funding round, valuing flexible workspace startup at $47 Billion.

timeline.title: Infamous S-1 Filing Exposed
timeline.description: Public S-1 document reveals massive operating losses ($1.6B loss on $1.8B revenue) and founder conflict-of-interest transactions.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Filing
timeline.description: WeWork files for Chapter 11 protection in New Jersey, seeking to reject over 60 expensive commercial leases.

keyTakeaways: Asset-liability duration mismatch: 15-year lease obligations vs 1-month member subscriptions.
Charismatic founder worship overriding basic unit economics oversight.
Aggressive growth metrics prioritized over cash flow profitability.

name: Bed Bath & Beyond
locationJurisdiction: Union, NJ (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D.N.J.)
primaryCause: E-Commerce Disruption & Private Label Blunder
sourceName: SEC EDGAR Form 8-K & Wall Street Journal
summary: Iconic home goods superstore ruined by a failed private-label inventory pivot, delayed e-commerce adoption, and reckless share buybacks that drained liquidity.
earlyWarningSignals: 2023-01-26: JPMorgan issues default notice on $550M revolving credit line.
2022-08-31: Announced closure of 150 store locations and 20% workforce layoff.
2022-06-29: CEO Mark Tritton ousted after same-store sales plunge 27%.

timeline.title: Peak Revenue & Share Buybacks
timeline.description: Bed Bath & Beyond executes over $11 Billion in stock buybacks instead of investing in digital supply chains.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 & Store Liquidation Sales
timeline.description: Company files Chapter 11 and announces closure of all 360 flagship stores.

keyTakeaways: Share buybacks drained cash reserves that were desperately needed for digital supply chain modernization.
Abrupt private label substitution shattered decades of consumer trust.
Coupon-driven store model failed to convert to modern digital loyalty programs.

name: Silicon Valley Bank (SVB)
locationJurisdiction: Santa Clara, CA (FDIC Receivership)
primaryCause: Duration Mismatch & Bank Run
sourceName: FDIC Receivership Order & Federal Reserve Review
summary: 16th largest US bank collapsed in 48 hours after surging interest rates crushed the value of its long-duration treasury bond portfolio, triggering a venture-led social media bank run.
earlyWarningSignals: 2023-03-08: Announced $1.8B realized loss on sale of $21B bond portfolio.
2022-04-29: Chief Risk Officer Laura Izurieta departed; position left vacant for 8 months.
2022-12-31: Unrealized losses on hold-to-maturity securities exceeded $15 Billion.

timeline.title: $42B Single-Day Digital Bank Run
timeline.description: Venture capitalists instruct portfolio founders to pull deposits; $42 Billion withdrawn in under 24 hours.

timeline.title: FDIC Receivership & Shutdown
timeline.description: California regulators close SVB and appoint FDIC receiver in 2nd largest US bank failure.

keyTakeaways: Concentration risk: 90%+ deposits uninsured and concentrated in tight-knit venture ecosystem.
Failure to hedge interest rate risk during rapid central bank tightening cycles.
Modern digital banking enabled unprecedented speed of deposit flight.

name: Spirit Airlines
locationJurisdiction: Miramar, FL (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D. Del.)
primaryCause: Blocked JetBlue Merger & Engine Recalls
summary: Ultra-low-cost carrier overwhelmed by debt after a federal judge blocked its $3.8B sale to JetBlue, compounded by Pratt & Whitney engine recall groundings and surging labor costs.
earlyWarningSignals: 2024-08-15: Auditor warns of debt refinancing wall with $1.1B loyalty bonds due 2025.
2024-03-04: JetBlue merger officially terminated following DOJ antitrust ruling.
2023-09-20: Pratt & Whitney engine powder defect grounds 25+ Spirit aircraft.

timeline.title: Federal Judge Blocks JetBlue Merger
timeline.description: US District Court blocks merger on antitrust grounds, causing Spirit stock to collapse by 60%.

timeline.title: Prearranged Chapter 11 Filing
timeline.description: Spirit files Chapter 11 to equitize $795M in bond debt while securing $350M in DIP financing.

keyTakeaways: Relying on regulatory approval for an exit strategy leaves high-leverage companies exposed.
Aircraft fleet groundings due to component defects severely restrict revenue generation.

name: Silicon Valley Bank (SVB Financial Group)
locationJurisdiction: Santa Clara, CA (U.S. Bankruptcy Court S.D.N.Y.)
primaryCause: Unhedged Interest Rate Risk & Tech Venture Deposit Run
summary: Premier venture capital lender failed in 48 hours after a $42B bank run triggered by unhedged long-duration Treasury bond losses as Fed interest rates rose.
earlyWarningSignals: 2023-03-08: SVB announces $1.8B loss on bond portfolio sale and attempts emergency $2.25B stock sale.
2023-03-09: Founders Fund and top VCs advise portfolio startups to withdraw cash immediately.
2023-01-19: Chief Risk Officer position left vacant for 8 consecutive months in 2022.

timeline.title: $1.8B Bond Loss & Capital Raise
timeline.description: SVB announces $1.8B net loss after selling $21B securities portfolio to meet withdrawals.

timeline.title: FDIC Seizure & Receivership
timeline.description: California regulators close SVB and place bank under FDIC receivership after $42B run.

keyTakeaways: Unhedged long-duration fixed-income portfolios create fatal asset-liability mismatches when rates rise.
Concentrated venture capital deposit bases can trigger digital bank runs in under 24 hours.

name: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc.
locationJurisdiction: Union, NJ (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D.N.J.)
primaryCause: Failed Private Label Strategy & Supplier Credit Cutoffs
summary: Iconic home goods retailer went bankrupt following a disastrous pivot to private label inventory, loss of national brand suppliers, and massive store closures.
earlyWarningSignals: 2023-01-05: SEC Form 8-K disclosure warning of bankruptcy filing due to credit line defaults.
2022-08-31: Announcement of 150 store closures and laying off 20% of corporate staff.
2022-06-29: Ouster of CEO Mark Tritton following 25% revenue decline.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Filing
timeline.description: Bed Bath & Beyond files Chapter 11 in New Jersey to begin winding down 360 stores.

keyTakeaways: Replacing trusted national brand inventory with unknown private label brands destroys customer loyalty.
Suppliers cutting off trade credit lines accelerates inventory depletion.

name: Yellow Corporation (Yellow Freight)
locationJurisdiction: Nashville, TN (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D. Del.)
primaryCause: Debt Overload, Failed Acquisition Integration & Teamsters Labor Strike
sourceName: SEC EDGAR Form 8-K & Fleet Auction Docket #23-11069
summary: 100-year-old American trucking giant ceased operations and liquidated its 12,000 trucks and 300 shipping terminals following a debt crisis and union standoff.
earlyWarningSignals: 2023-07-30: Ceased operations and laid off 30,000 workers ahead of bankruptcy.
2023-06-27: Lawsuit filed against International Brotherhood of Teamsters alleging blocked restructuring.
2020-07-01: Secured controversial $700M U.S. Treasury national security loan.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Fleet Liquidation
timeline.description: Yellow files Chapter 11 seeking approval to auction 300 shipping terminals and 12,000 trucks.

keyTakeaways: Acquiring competitors without integrating IT systems creates redundant cost structures.
Unresolved labor disputes combined with debt walls lead to immediate operational shutdown.

name: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc.
locationJurisdiction: New York, NY (U.S. Bankruptcy Court S.D.N.Y.)
primaryCause: Subprime Mortgage Exposure & Extreme Balance Sheet Leverage (31x)
summary: Largest bankruptcy filing in U.S. history ($639B debt). 158-year-old investment bank collapsed from subprime mortgage debt leverage, triggering the 2008 Global Financial Crisis.
earlyWarningSignals: 2008-09-10: Pre-announces $3.9B Q3 loss and plan to sell majority stake in Neuberger Berman.
2008-06-09: Stock drops 11% after rival firms cut credit lines.
2007-08-01: Closes BNC Mortgage subprime lending unit.

timeline.title: Largest Bankruptcy in US History
timeline.description: Lehman files Chapter 11 with $639B liabilities after Fed and Treasury decline bailout.

keyTakeaways: 31x leverage leaves zero buffer against asset impairment.
Commercial paper and repo market liquidity can evaporate overnight.

name: Enron Corporation
locationJurisdiction: Houston, TX (U.S. Bankruptcy Court S.D.N.Y.)
primaryCause: Mark-to-Market Accounting Fraud & Off-Balance-Sheet SPEs
summary: America's 7th largest company collapsed after whistleblowers and regulators exposed off-balance-sheet Special Purpose Entities (SPEs) used to hide billions in losses.
earlyWarningSignals: 2001-10-16: Announces $618M Q3 loss and $1.2B equity reduction.
2001-08-14: CEO Jeffrey Skilling abruptly resigns citing personal reasons.
2001-03-05: Fortune magazine publishes 'Is Enron Overpriced?' by Bethany McLean.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Filing
timeline.description: Enron files Chapter 11 after Dynegy merger agreement falls through.

keyTakeaways: Off-balance-sheet entities used to hide debt inevitably trigger catastrophic restatements.
Mark-to-market accounting on unearned future revenues masks real cash flow insolvency.

name: Washington Mutual (WaMu)
locationJurisdiction: Seattle, WA (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D. Del.)
primaryCause: Subprime Option-ARM Mortgage Default Run
summary: Largest bank failure in American history ($307B assets). WaMu seized by OTS/FDIC following a $16.7B deposit run triggered by catastrophic subprime Option-ARM mortgage portfolio defaults.
earlyWarningSignals: 2008-09-15: Credit rating agencies downgrade WaMu debt to junk status.
2008-09-08: Ouster of long-time CEO Kerry Killinger.
2008-04-08: TPG leads emergency $7.2B capital injection.

timeline.title: Largest Bank Seizure in US History
timeline.description: Office of Thrift Supervision seizes WaMu and sells banking assets to JPMorgan Chase for $1.9B.

keyTakeaways: Aggressive subprime Option-ARM lending creates catastrophic credit losses when housing prices drop.
Retail deposit runs accelerate rapidly when debt rating agencies downgrade bank debt to junk.

name: General Motors Corporation (Old GM)
locationJurisdiction: Detroit, MI (U.S. Bankruptcy Court S.D.N.Y.)
primaryCause: Legacy Pension Liabilities, SUV Sales Collapse & GFC Credit Freeze
summary: America's largest automaker filed for Chapter 11 in the 4th largest bankruptcy in U.S. history ($172B liabilities), resulting in a $50B U.S. Treasury bailout and 'New GM' restructuring.
earlyWarningSignals: 2009-03-30: Obama Administration Auto Taskforce rejects GM restructuring plan.
2008-11-07: Warns cash reserves are insufficient to operate through 2009.
2005-03-16: S&P downgrades GM debt to junk status.

timeline.title: Government Supervised Chapter 11
timeline.description: Old GM files Chapter 11 petition with $172B liabilities, receiving $30B additional Treasury DIP financing.

keyTakeaways: Unfunded legacy healthcare and pension liabilities create crippling fixed-cost burdens during auto downturns.
Section 363 sale structures can isolate bad assets into legacy liquidation trusts while preserving viable core brands.

name: Bear Stearns Companies Inc.
locationJurisdiction: New York, NY (Federal Reserve Board Order)
primaryCause: High-Grade Subprime Hedge Fund Collapses & Overnight Repo Lockup
sourceName: Fed Maiden Lane I Facility & JP Morgan Acquisition Agreement
summary: Wall Street investment bank collapsed in 72 hours as counterparties refused repo financing following the collapse of its two subprime mortgage hedge funds.
earlyWarningSignals: 2008-03-13: Bear Stearns informs Fed its liquidity reserves are exhausted.
2007-07-17: Pledges $1.6B to bail out two internal subprime hedge funds before liquidating them.
2007-06-22: Merrill Lynch seizes $850M in Bear Stearns hedge fund collateral.

timeline.title: Fed Emergency Rescue & JPMorgan Sale
timeline.description: JPMorgan Chase agrees to acquire Bear Stearns for $2/share (later raised to $10/share) backed by $29B Fed Maiden Lane guaranty.

keyTakeaways: Relying on short-term overnight repo markets to fund illiquid subprime assets exposes firms to instant insolvency.
Central bank emergency lending facilities (Maiden Lane) are used when counterparty systemic contagion threatens markets.

name: CIT Group Inc.
locationJurisdiction: New York, NY (U.S. Bankruptcy Court S.D.N.Y.)
primaryCause: Commercial Paper Market Lockup & Subprime Student/Middle-Market Loan Losses
summary: 100-year-old middle-market commercial lender filed the 5th largest bankruptcy in U.S. history ($71B liabilities) after commercial paper markets froze during the 2008 financial crisis.
earlyWarningSignals: 2009-07-15: Rescue talks with U.S. Treasury fail after TARP funds exhausted.
2009-07-20: Bondholders provide $3B emergency credit line.
2008-12-31: Receives $2.33B in TARP preferred stock capital.

timeline.title: Prepackaged Chapter 11 Filing
timeline.description: CIT Group files prepackaged Chapter 11 reducing debt by $10.5B and eliminating TARP equity.

keyTakeaways: Middle-market lenders dependent on wholesale short-term paper cannot survive credit market freezes.
Prepackaged Chapter 11 plans allow solvent operations to emerge swiftly with reduced debt.

name: Circuit City Stores, Inc.
locationJurisdiction: Richmond, VA (U.S. Bankruptcy Court E.D. Va.)
ceoAtFailure: Philip J. Schoonover / James A. Marcum
primaryCause: Fired Experienced Store Staff, Best Buy Competition & Credit Line Cutoff
summary: 2nd largest US electronics retailer liquidated all 567 stores after firing 3,400 senior commissioned salespeople to cut costs, destroying customer service ahead of the 2008 holiday season.
earlyWarningSignals: 2007-03-28: Fired 3,400 highest-paid experienced sales associates to replace with lower-wage workers.
2008-11-03: Announces closure of 155 store locations and lay off of 17% of workforce.
2008-09-26: Trade credit insurers withdraw coverage for inventory shipments.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Liquidation Filing
timeline.description: Circuit City files Chapter 11 seeking buyer, converting to total store liquidation in Jan 2009.

keyTakeaways: Firing knowledgeable sales staff to cut short-term wages destroys retail brand equity and revenue.
Failing to adapt store formats against competitors like Best Buy and Amazon leads to rapid inventory obsolescence.

name: Hertz Global Holdings, Inc.
locationJurisdiction: Estero, FL (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D. Del.)
primaryCause: COVID Travel Shutdown & Asset-Backed Fleet Securitization Debt Wall
summary: 102-year-old car rental giant filed Chapter 11 after pandemic travel bans wiped out airport revenue, triggering defaults on its $14.4B fleet lease securitization debt.
earlyWarningSignals: 2020-04-29: Hertz misses operating lease payments on asset-backed fleet vehicles.
2020-03-20: Layoff of 12,000 employees following 80% drop in airport rentals.
2020-05-18: CEO Kathryn Marinello resigns 4 days before bankruptcy filing.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Filing
timeline.description: Hertz files Chapter 11 in Delaware with $19B debt, initiating fleet liquidation negotiations.

keyTakeaways: Asset-backed vehicle securitization structures require continuous operating cash flow to avoid margin calls.
Extreme macroeconomic demand shocks like global travel shutdowns instantly collapse high-fixed-cost fleet operators.

name: FTX Trading Ltd. (Alameda Research)
locationJurisdiction: Nassau, Bahamas (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D. Del.)
ceoAtFailure: Sam Bankman-Fried / John J. Ray III
primaryCause: Co-mingling Customer Funds, Alameda Leverage & Lack of Internal Controls
sourceName: U.S. Bankruptcy Court D. Del. Docket #22-11068
summary: 3rd largest global crypto exchange collapsed in 5 days after a $6B deposit run exposed an $8.7B hole caused by illegal transfer of customer funds to sister hedge fund Alameda Research.
earlyWarningSignals: 2022-11-02: CoinDesk leaks Alameda Research balance sheet showing massive FTT token concentration.
2022-11-06: Binance CEO CZ announces liquidation of all remaining FTT holdings.
2022-11-08: FTX halts customer withdrawals as run exceeds $6B in 72 hours.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Filing & SBF Resignation
timeline.description: FTX, Alameda Research, and 130 affiliated entities file Chapter 11; restructuring expert John J. Ray III appointed CEO.

keyTakeaways: Co-mingling exchange customer deposits with proprietary trading funds is illegal and fatal.
Using illiquid exchange-issued tokens (FTT) as collateral for multibillion-dollar loans leads to immediate liquidation when prices drop.

name: Celsius Network LLC
locationJurisdiction: Hoboken, NJ (U.S. Bankruptcy Court S.D.N.Y.)
primaryCause: High-Yield Staking Mismatch, Terra/Luna Exposure & Liquidity Run
summary: Major crypto lending platform promising 18% APY froze all withdrawals following the $40B collapse of Terra/Luna and unhedged DeFi liquidation calls.
earlyWarningSignals: 2022-06-12: Pauses all customer withdrawals, swaps, and transfers citing 'extreme market conditions'.
2022-05-11: $500M+ lost in Terra (LUNA/UST) algorithmic stablecoin depeg.
2021-11-26: Celsius CFO arrested in Israel in connection with prior ICO fraud.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Restructuring Filing
timeline.description: Celsius Network files Chapter 11 in New York showing $1.2B balance sheet deficit.

keyTakeaways: Promising 18% yields on liquid deposits requires taking extreme unhedged risk in illiquid DeFi protocols.
Terms of Service claiming ownership of deposited assets leave retail users as unsecured creditors in Chapter 11.

name: First Republic Bank
locationJurisdiction: San Francisco, CA (FDIC Receivership Order)
primaryCause: Uninsured Wealthy Deposit Run & Low-Rate Jumbo Mortgage Impairment
sourceName: FDIC Press Release PR-34-2023 & JPMorgan Acquisition
summary: 2nd largest bank failure in U.S. history ($229B assets). Wealthy client bank suffered a $100B deposit run in Q1 2023 following SVB's collapse, leading to FDIC seizure and sale to JPMorgan Chase.
earlyWarningSignals: 2023-04-24: Q1 earnings report reveals $102B net deposit flight.
2023-03-16: 11 major U.S. banks deposit $30B emergency liquidity to stabilize First Republic.
2023-03-15: S&P and Fitch downgrade First Republic rating to junk.

timeline.title: FDIC Seizure & JPMorgan Acquisition
timeline.description: FDIC takes possession of First Republic and sells all deposits and $203B assets to JPMorgan Chase.

keyTakeaways: High concentration of uninsured deposits (>68%) creates extreme run vulnerability.
Long-term low-rate jumbo mortgages lose substantial market value when benchmark rates rise 500 bps.

name: Express, Inc. (Bonobos)
locationJurisdiction: Columbus, OH (U.S. Bankruptcy Court D. Del.)
primaryCause: Mall Foot Traffic Decline, Debt Overhang & Failed E-Commerce Pivot
summary: Popular mall apparel retailer Express filed Chapter 11 in April 2024 seeking court approval to close 100 stores and sell assets to a consortium led by WHP Global.
earlyWarningSignals: 2024-02-14: Delisted from the New York Stock Exchange due to low stock price.
2023-11-28: Express reports Q3 net loss of $36.8M and warns of liquidity constraints.
2023-04-13: Acquired menswear brand Bonobos from Walmart for $75M.

timeline.title: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Filing
timeline.description: Express files Chapter 11 in Delaware with $1.2B debt, securing $49M DIP financing.

keyTakeaways: Heavy reliance on traditional suburban shopping mall foot traffic creates persistent sales drag.
Digital DTC acquisitions cannot compensate for over-stored physical retail footprints.
